```{r}
text <- readLines("jus2026adult.txt", warn = FALSE)
# -------------------------------
# EXTRACT NAMES
# -------------------------------

# Pattern: two consecutive capitalized words (handles hyphens + accents)
pattern <- "\\b[A-ZÅÄÖ][a-zåäöA-ZÅÄÖ\\-]+\\s+[A-ZÅÄÖ][a-zåäöA-ZÅÄÖ\\-]+"

matches <- gregexpr(pattern, text, perl = TRUE)
names <- regmatches(text, matches)[[1]]

# -------------------------------
# CLEAN (remove header junk if any)
# -------------------------------
author_names <- unique(names)
# Remove header / obvious junk
author_names <- author_names[!grepl("Apurahansaaja|Stipendiat|Tutkimuslaitos|Forskningsinstitut|Määrä|Belopp|Vuotta|År", author_names)]

# Optional: remove entries that have only one word (like "Pirjo Oulun", "Oscar HUS")
author_names <- author_names[sapply(strsplit(author_names, " "), length) == 2]

# Preview
print(author_names)
length(author_names)
```

```{r}
# ================================
# FULL COAUTHORSHIP PIPELINE (R)
# ================================

# Install packages if needed
packages <- c("httr", "jsonlite", "dplyr", "purrr")
installed <- packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())
if (any(!installed)) install.packages(packages[!installed])

library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# -------------------------------
# INPUT: list of author names
# -------------------------------
#author_names <- c("John Smith", "Jane Doe")

# -------------------------------
# FUNCTION: search author in OpenAlex
# -------------------------------
search_author <- function(name) {
  url <- paste0("https://api.openalex.org/authors?search=", URLencode(name))
  res <- httr::GET(url)
  data <- jsonlite::fromJSON(httr::content(res, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))
  
  # Handle empty results safely
  if (length(data$results) == 0) {
    cat("No results for:", name, "\n")
    return(data.frame(id=NA, display_name=NA, works_count=NA))
  }
  
  # Convert results to a proper data.frame
  df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(data$results, function(x) {
    data.frame(
      id = x$id,
      display_name = x$display_name,
      works_count = x$works_count,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
  return(df)
}
# -------------------------------
# STEP 1: resolve names → author IDs
# -------------------------------
author_ids <- c()

for (name in author_names) {
  cat("\nSearching for:", name, "\n")
  results <- search_author(name)
  print(results)
  
  if (all(is.na(results$id))) next  # skip names with no match
  
  # Pick the first result automatically (or choose manually)
  author_ids <- c(author_ids, results$id[1])
}

# -------------------------------
# FUNCTION: get ALL papers (with pagination)
# -------------------------------
get_all_papers <- function(author_id) {
  papers <- list()
  cursor <- "*"
  
  repeat {
    url <- paste0(
      "https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=author.id:", author_id,
      "&per-page=200&cursor=", cursor
    )
    
    res <- GET(url)
    data <- fromJSON(content(res, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
    
    papers <- append(papers, data$results)
    
    if (is.null(data$meta$next_cursor)) break
    cursor <- data$meta$next_cursor
  }
  
  papers
}

# -------------------------------
# STEP 2: get papers for ALL authors
# -------------------------------
all_papers <- list()

for (aid in author_ids) {
  cat("\nFetching papers for:", aid, "\n")
  papers <- get_all_papers(aid)
  all_papers <- append(all_papers, papers)
}

# -------------------------------
# STEP 3: extract coauthors per paper
# -------------------------------
author_lists <- lapply(all_papers, function(p) {
  
  if (!is.list(p) || is.null(p$authorships)) return(NULL)
  
  authors <- sapply(p$authorships, function(a) {
    if (!is.null(a$author) && !is.null(a$author$display_name)) {
      a$author$display_name
    } else {
      NA
    }
  })
  
  authors <- na.omit(authors)
  
  if (length(authors) < 2) return(NULL)  # skip single-author papers
  
  return(authors)
})

# Clean NULLs
author_lists <- author_lists[!sapply(author_lists, is.null)]
# -------------------------------
# STEP 4: build pairwise edges
# -------------------------------
edges <- do.call(rbind, lapply(author_lists, function(authors) {
  authors <- unique(authors)
  if (length(authors) < 2) return(NULL)
  t(combn(authors, 2))
}))

edges_df <- as.data.frame(edges)
colnames(edges_df) <- c("author1", "author2")

# -------------------------------
# STEP 5: compute weights
# -------------------------------
edges_weighted <- edges_df %>%
  count(author1, author2, name = "weight")

# -------------------------------
# OUTPUT
# -------------------------------
print(head(edges_weighted))

# Save to file
write.csv(edges_weighted, "coauthorship_network.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nDone! File saved as 'coauthorship_network.csv'\n")
```





```{r}
# ================================
# 📦 Install & load packages
# ================================
install.packages(c("igraph", "ggraph", "tidygraph", "dplyr", "ggplot2"))

library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(tidygraph)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ================================
# 📥 INPUT: your edge list
# ================================
# edges_weighted must have:
# author1 | author2 | weight

# Example (remove if you already have data):
# edges_weighted <- data.frame(
#   author1 = c("A","A","B","C"),
#   author2 = c("B","C","C","D"),
#   weight = c(3,2,1,4)
# )

# ================================
# 🧠 Build graph
# ================================
g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges_weighted, directed = FALSE)

# ================================
# 📊 Centrality measures
# ================================
V(g)$degree <- degree(g)
V(g)$betweenness <- betweenness(g, normalized = TRUE)
V(g)$closeness <- closeness(g, normalized = TRUE)
V(g)$eigen <- eigen_centrality(g)$vector

# ================================
# 🧩 Community detection
# ================================
communities <- cluster_louvain(g)
V(g)$community <- membership(communities)

# ================================
# 🧹 Optional: filter low-degree nodes
# ================================
g <- delete_vertices(g, degree(g) < 2)

# ================================
# 🔄 Convert for ggraph
# ================================
tg <- as_tbl_graph(g)

# ================================
# 🎨 Visualization
# ================================
gg <- ggraph(tg, layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(aes(width = weight), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_node_point(aes(size = degree, color = as.factor(community))) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +
  theme_void()

# ================================
# 🔍 Top central authors
# ================================
cat("\nTop Degree (most collaborators):\n")
print(sort(V(g)$degree, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10])

cat("\nTop Betweenness (key connectors):\n")
print(sort(V(g)$betweenness, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10])

cat("\nTop Closeness (most reachable):\n")
print(sort(V(g)$closeness, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10])

cat("\nTop Eigenvector (most influential):\n")
print(sort(V(g)$eigen, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10])

# ================================
# 💾 Optional: export for Gephi
# ================================
write_graph(g, file = "coauthorship_network.gml", format = "gml")
```

```{r}
centrality_df <- data.frame(
  author = V(g)$name,
  degree = degree(g),
  betweenness = betweenness(g, normalized = TRUE),
  closeness = closeness(g, normalized = TRUE),
  eigenvector = eigen_centrality(g)$vector
)

# Order by each centrality measure and show top 10
top_degree       <- head(centrality_df[order(-centrality_df$degree), ], 10)
top_betweenness  <- head(centrality_df[order(-centrality_df$betweenness), ], 10)
top_closeness    <- head(centrality_df[order(-centrality_df$closeness), ], 10)
top_eigenvector  <- head(centrality_df[order(-centrality_df$eigenvector), ], 10)
```
